statement_or_entity: Before combining atmospheric data, reconcile variable definition, physical units, coordinates, calendar, time reference, sign convention, support, and aggregation interval.
A time coordinate comparison must preserve the reference datetime, calendar, time zone or UTC basis, and whether values are instantaneous, averaged, or accumulated.
A remotely retrieved geophysical variable must be described separately from the instrument signal and must carry retrieval assumptions, priors, ancillary inputs, sensitivity, and quality screening.
Validation must not treat the reference dataset or instrument as error-free; its uncertainty, representativeness, support, and shared inputs must be included in interpretation.
A forecast skill or improvement claim must name the forecast object, verification sample, metric orientation, baseline, and uncertainty.
Ensemble members, related models, overlapping forecast windows, repeated stations, and spatial samples must not be treated as independent without a defensible dependence model.
An association or predictive relationship does not establish a causal effect without an explicit estimand, identification assumptions, confounder strategy, and sensitivity analysis.

statement_or_entity: A model comparison must report version, grid and effective resolution, vertical coordinate, forcing, initialization, boundary conditions, parameterizations, ensemble design, post-processing, and verification data when relevant.
Research data, code, and workflows should use persistent identifiers, rich metadata, qualified links, licenses, provenance, and domain standards sufficient for discovery and reuse.
A conclusion must remain bounded by the sampled region, period, atmospheric regime, scale, study design, data coverage, and quantified uncertainty.
